name: Brow slitting / cuts
lead: Brow slitting, also called eyebrow slits or brow cuts, is a grooming style in which one or more thin lines are shaved or cut through the eyebrow hair so that bare skin shows in a short vertical or diagonal gap. It is purely a hair-styling choice and is usually done with a razor or trimmer; it does not involve cutting skin.

Wikipedia's general article on eyebrows notes that shaving lines into the eyebrows was popular among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s, and cites a 2008 news report that linked the trend to gang concerns in schools [1]. Beyond that mention, little encyclopedic or scientific material exists on the style itself, so this article is short.
infobox: Hair shaved or trimmed from the brow
Popular among some youth in the 1990s and 2000s [1]

paras: The style removes a narrow strip of hair across the brow, most often near the tail or arch, leaving a visible gap. Variations include a single slit, multiple slits, or a diagonal cut. Because only hair is removed, the gap fills in as the hair regrows.

Brow shaping more broadly (plucking, waxing, threading, trimming and tinting) is a long-established grooming practice, and fashions in eyebrow shape have changed repeatedly over time, from the shaved and repainted brows of Japanese hikimayu to the thin plucked brows of the 1920s and 1930s [1].

The Wikipedia article on eyebrows reports that shaved lines in the brow were popular among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s, and mentions a 2008 news report connecting the look to gang-related concerns in schools [1]. The article gives no further detail, and the available sources do not describe how widely such associations were held.

Brow slits are generally treated in appearance communities as a style choice rather than a facial-structure change. Discussion of eyebrows in looksmaxxing spaces more often concerns shape, density and the eye area, and no published studies examine how slits affect perceived attractiveness.

card.summary: A shaved gap cut through the eyebrow as a style statement; temporary, cosmetic, and barely studied.
card.note: No published research on the style; the main practical limit is that the hair regrows.

quick.overview:
Brow slitting is a grooming style where a thin line of hair is shaved out of the eyebrow. It has been popular with some young people since at least the 1990s and is a fashion choice rather than a structural change.

Sources on the style are thin. Encyclopedias mention it only briefly, and no studies have tested its effect on how a face is perceived.
quick.mechanism: Hair is trimmed or shaved from a narrow strip of the brow with a razor or trimmer, leaving bare skin visible. Nothing is done to the skin or follicle, so the gap grows back.
quick.risks: Shaving carries the usual minor risks of razor use such as nicks or irritation. A 2008 news report cited by Wikipedia linked the style to gang concerns in some schools, which can matter where school or workplace dress rules apply.
